question: Does every real matrix have real eigenvectors?
expanded_answer: Some real matrices, such as a nontrivial 2D rotation, have no real direction that maps back onto itself. In those cases, real eigenvectors may not exist, and complex eigenvalues/eigenvectors or another viewpoint is needed.
key_points: Real matrices may lack real eigenvectors
common_wrong_ideas: Assuming every matrix has a real eigenvector
Expecting rotation matrices to preserve a real line
